subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory audio support be narrowed to raw MP3/WAV inputs, or should OpenClaw add a maintained transcoding path for OGG/Opus and other audio formats?
rationale: Current code and docs promise OGG/Opus audio indexing, but satisfying that promise requires either narrowing the public contract or adding media transcoding, which is a product/dependency/security choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Narrow To Provider-Supported Audio
options.body: Filter or skip non-MP3/WAV audio for Gemini embeddings with a diagnostic and update docs/tests to match the upstream contract.

options.title: Add Managed Transcoding
options.body: Convert unsupported audio to WAV or MP3 before embedding, accepting the added dependency, platform, and security review burden.

options.title: Docs-Only Limitation
options.body: Document that users must convert unsupported audio themselves, leaving current runtime behavior mostly unchanged except for clearer expectations.

recommendation.title: Narrow To Provider-Supported Audio
recommendation.body: Filter or skip non-MP3/WAV audio for Gemini embeddings with a diagnostic and update docs/tests to match the upstream contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the multimodal memory feature and public config/docs boundary introduced by the merged image/audio indexing work.
